date_note: Date is iXBT's article (23 November); the page gives no earlier day for F6's finding.
exec: F6 says fraudsters now add deepfakes built from victims' own photos to fake court summonses, a lure meant to push people into calling a scam call centre.
geo_basis: victims in Russia as the source states; country centroid used
plain: According to the security firm F6, scammers send Russians fake court summonses from the bailiff service, then claim their government account was hacked. F6 says they now also use deepfakes made from victims' photos.
summary: According to F6, as reported by iXBT, scammers send Russians messages in the name of the bailiff service (FSSP) summoning them to court; a fake case page asks for a code, then claims their state-portal account was hacked and gives a fraudsters' 'support' number. F6 says the scheme uses data from old leaks and, for the first time in it, deepfakes built from victims' photos, including passport photos.
title: F6: scammers impersonate Russia's bailiff service with fake court summonses and victims' deepfakes

validation.note: Single source: iXBT relays F6's findings; F6's own publication was not found or read.

key_findings: Fake FSSP messages summon victims to court; the attached 'PDF' links to a fake court-case site.
Victims are told their state-portal account was hacked and given a fraudsters' phone number; a Telegram stage follows.
F6 says deepfakes from victims' photos are used in this scheme for the first time.
